newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma police bar access to Suu Kyi's residence.
newsitem.headline: Burma police bar access to Suu Kyi's residence.

text.p: Burmese police on Friday blocked the main road leading to the residence of democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi on Friday where her National League for Democracy had planned to hold a congress, witnesses said.
"They are trying to prevent our congress from taking place," said an NLD party member, who was standing near a roadblock erected along University Avenue where Suu Kyi's house is located.
Police refused to let people or vehicles gather in the vicinity of her home and diverted traffic to other roads, witnesses added.

NLD party sources told Reuters they had heard that police planned to prevent anyone from gathering near Suu Kyi's home where a congress of about 200 of the NLD's key members had been planned from Friday to Sunday.
A plan to hold a similar gathering in May spurred the arrest of some 260 democracy activists by the military government.
The ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) later released the detainees.
So far, this time, the SLORC had not arrested any NLD supporters, NLD sources said.
The scene at Suu Kyi's house was quiet with nobody gathering outside her home, although some NLD members were inside, witnesses added.
There were many NLD party flags flying prominently around the compound in Suu Kyi's lakeside home to mark the congress.
Repeated attempts to reach Suu Kyi's home by telephone to obtain comments from her or senior party officials failed.

The NLD, which won a landslide victory in a 1990 general election that was never recognised by the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC), tried to hold its first-ever gathering of elected representatives in late May.
One diplomat said the upcoming party meeting would be a test of how serious the SLORC was in its desire to gag Suu Kyi who has continued to push for more democracy in Burma.
He said the planned congress would clearly be seen as a challenge to the SLORC but government reaction had been muted so far.
